# clinique

<!-- badges: start -->
<!-- badges: end -->

This package gives you data shaped like a real clinical trial, so you can fit
that trial's own analysis to it. Each dataset is modeled on a published
trial and its statistical analysis plan: the same visits, the same
covariates, and effects that match the published results.

Every subject is made up. The data is not affiliated with or endorsed by
any trial's sponsor.

## Installation

You can install the development version of clinique from
[GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("edgararuiz/clinique")
```

## Available studies

Each study has its own function. There are three so far, all trials of
drugs that lower LDL cholesterol. All are analyzed with a mixed model for
repeated measures (MMRM), but each one teaches something different:

| Function | Trial | Drug | Subjects | Design | What it teaches |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `simulate_orion10()` | ORION-10 | Inclisiran, twice a year | 1,561 | 1:1, 6 visits over 18 months | An effect that rises and falls with each dose |
| `simulate_orion11()` | ORION-11 | Inclisiran, twice a year | 1,617 | 1:1, 7 visits over 18 months | A sister trial of ORION-10 whose analysis plan adds a covariate and keeps Day 90 in the model |
| `simulate_odyssey_lt()` | ODYSSEY LONG TERM | Alirocumab, every two weeks | 2,341 | 2:1, 7 visits over 1 year | Adjusting for randomization strata, and weighting means by them |

The difference in dosing shows in the data. Inclisiran's effect is
strongest a few months after each dose and weaker just before the next.
Alirocumab's stays flat:

```{r profiles, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 3.5, fig.alt = "Mean percent change in LDL by study day for each arm. ORION-10's inclisiran arm rises and falls between doses; ODYSSEY LONG TERM's alirocumab arm stays flat near -63%. Both placebo arms stay near zero."}
library(clinique)

set.seed(1)
studies <- list(
  "ORION-10" = simulate_orion10(1561),
  "ODYSSEY LONG TERM" = simulate_odyssey_lt(2341)
)

old <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))
for (name in names(studies)) {
  d <- studies[[name]]
  means <- aggregate(ldl_pct_change ~ day + treatment, data = d, FUN = mean)
  plot(
    NULL,
    xlim = c(0, max(d$day)),
    ylim = c(-75, 10),
    xlab = "Study day",
    ylab = "Mean % change in LDL",
    main = name
  )
  abline(h = 0, col = "grey80")
  for (arm in levels(d$treatment)) {
    m <- means[means$treatment == arm, ]
    lines(c(0, m$day), c(0, m$ldl_pct_change), type = "b", pch = 19,
      col = if (arm == "Placebo") "grey50" else "steelblue")
  }
  legend("right", legend = rev(levels(d$treatment)), bty = "n",
    col = c("steelblue", "grey50"), lty = 1, pch = 19)
}
par(old)
```

## Example

Simulate ODYSSEY LONG TERM. Each row is one subject at one visit. The last
four columns are the randomization strata, which the trial's analysis
plan adjusts for:

```{r}
library(clinique)

set.seed(1)
ldl <- simulate_odyssey_lt(2341)
head(ldl)
```

Fit the trial's MMRM and compare the arms at Week 24, the primary
endpoint:

```{r}
fit <- mmrm::mmrm(
  ldl_pct_change ~ treatment * visit +
    hefh * visit +
    prior_mi_stroke * visit +
    statin_intensity * visit +
    region * visit +
    ldl_baseline * visit +
    us(visit | subject_id),
  data = ldl,
  reml = TRUE,
  method = "Satterthwaite"
)

means <- emmeans::emmeans(fit, ~ treatment | visit, weights = "proportional")
diffs <- summary(emmeans::contrast(means, "revpairwise"))
diffs[diffs$visit == "Week 24", ]
```

The trial reported a difference of -62% (95% CI -64 to -59).

## Learn more

Each study has an article that explains every number in the simulation,
where it came from, and what was assumed:

1. ORION-10: `vignette("orion10", package = "clinique")`.
2. ORION-11: `vignette("orion11", package = "clinique")`.
3. ODYSSEY LONG TERM: `vignette("odyssey-lt", package = "clinique")`.
